note: The shape library's comparison (stage 3b of specula-formae): the same props built through the engine by a cold agent, in three arms on two builds of the engine. 'none': an engine built without the shape library (the executable the command line gives as --exe base=PATH), and a brief with no word of a library. 'found': the engine with the library and its pointers (--exe library=PATH: model_build's description, the modelling family's catalog line, a project's notes/how.md and the brief at the first call), and the same brief as 'none' to the byte: it measures whether a cold agent finds the library by the engine's own pointers. 'told': the same engine, and a brief that names the library and its two calls. Each is measured against 'none'. Run with --data evals/leverage-props (docs/design/LEVERAGE.md, 'Another data folder'); 'examen leverage prompt --data evals/leverage-props' prints what each builder is told.

arms.name: none
text: - You build the props with the Specula engine. Your work folder is a Specula project made by the engine (`specula new`). Models are recipes (JSON) that the engine builds: its documents are in {docs} (`design/PROCEDURAL_MODELLING.md` for recipes).

- An engine left running, with its tools: start it with `{tool} engine start {run}` and stop it with `{tool} engine stop {run}`; call a tool with `{tool} call {run} TOOL '{{json}}'` or `TOOL @args.json` (`model_build` builds a recipe and reports its triangles, bounds and whether it is closed; `sight_frame` and `studio_sheet` take pictures; `{tool} tools {run} [FILTER]` lists the tools). The engine starts with no window. Never run the engine's executable yourself.
- Whoever checks the props starts with no engine running: the commands in your README must work from there.

rules: Someone may be using this machine: open no window that takes the keyboard or comes to the front, and never move the pointer or press keys for them.
Anything you start that listens, listens on 127.0.0.1 only.
Stop every process you started before you finish.
